title: Reversal of Paid Rental Benefits — Rental Reimbursement Coverage Accounting Note
content:
A Rental Reimbursement Coverage benefit payment is reversed at most once. A reversal is made for a duplicate invoice, an agency credit, or days outside the eligible period, for the amount of the days concerned.

## Elements of a reversal

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Reasons | A duplicate invoice; an agency credit; days outside the eligible period |
| Amount | The amount of the days concerned |
| Frequency | One reversal at most for any one benefit payment |
| Record tested | Whether a reversal is already recorded against that same benefit payment, on the company's records |

The rental benefits shown on a coverage are the benefits paid net of reversals: each reversal reduces them by its amount.

## Points of judgement

- *A benefit payment already carries a reversal.* It is not reversed again; the limit of one reversal is reached.
- *Two different benefit payments on the same claim.* Each is a separate payment, and each may carry its own single reversal.
- *Part of an invoice period falls outside the eligible period.* The reversal is for the amount of the days concerned, not the whole payment.

## Hypothetical example

A network invoice paid 5 rental days at USD 40.00 a day, USD 200.00 in all, and 2 of those days fall outside the eligible period. The reversal is for the amount of the 2 days concerned, USD 80.00, and the rental benefits on the coverage fall by USD 80.00. A second reversal of that same payment is not made.
